item.title: Novak wins Mexico Open for first solo PGA Tour win
item.description: Andrew Novak had previously triumphed at the 2025 Zurich Classic pairs event in New Orleans (Jonathan Bachman) Andrew Novak cruised to victory at the Mexico Open on Sunday, firing a two-under-par 69 to win by five strokes and claim his first individual title on the PGA Tour. The 31-year-old American converted his commanding overnight lead into a comfortable victory at Vidanta Vallarta with three straight birdies on the back nine. Novak, whose only previous tour victory came at last year's Zurich Classic pairs event alongside Ben Griffin, finished on a tournament record 25-under-par 259. "It is nice to get one. Obviously I loved Zurich and everything about that tournament -- it's so fun -- but it is nice to have one by myself too," said Novak. "This is one I've been working for for a while." Leading by six going into the final day, Novak started his final round steadily, with seven pars, before a birdie on the eighth. He had a slight stumble at the turn, missing a four-foot putt on 10 for his first bogey since Friday. But he snuffed out any hope for the chasing pack with a string of three consecutive birdies from the 12th onward. That included a 14-foot putt on the par-three 13th, and then a huge 44-foot roller on the 14th green that boosted his lead back to five over Doug Ghim. "Ten was a mistake. Just, I don't know, got lackadaisical there, three terrible shots in a row, but recovered, made three birdies in a row, 12, 13, 14. And that really kind of settled everything," said Novak. When Ghim bogeyed the 14th, Novak's lead grew to six. The American looked relaxed as he racked up pars on 15 and 16 before missing a short par putt on 17. His par on 18 was enough to beat the tournament record of 24-under-par, after scorching rounds of 61 and 62 on Friday and Saturday respectively. "Just happy with how I played today. I thought I grinded out pretty well," said the winner. Steven Fisk and Norway's Kristoffer Ventura were second-placed on 20-under-par 264, followed by Ben Griffin and Canada's Mackenzie Hughes on 265. Matthieu Pavon of France had begun Sunday in second place, but slipped out of the top 10 with three bogeys down the back nine. A rough finish could have been even worse for the Frenchman, as long grass by the 18th green barely stopped his ball finding the water, and he saved par. Ghim, who started Sunday in third, finished tied-sixth with a double bogey on 18. amz/js

item.title: Antonelli becomes world champion as Verstappen wins in Mexico
item.description: Kimi Antonelli did not win the race in Mexico City - but he did not need to [Getty Images] Kimi Antonelli clinched his first world title and became the youngest champion in Formula 1 history by finishing third at the Mexico City Grand Prix. Antonelli - 20 years and 68 days old - finished the race in third, behind Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton. His moment of glory came on a day when tensions at Ferrari between seven-time champion Hamilton and team-mate Charles Leclerc came close to boiling over. Antonelli drove a composed race amid some hectic action involving the other front-runners in a grand prix interrupted by a red flag that led to a 25-lap sprint to the finish. The Italian, a teenager until late August, spent the closing laps watching Hamilton try to get close enough to pass Verstappen after the two had made contact at the first chicane at the restart. But Hamilton found it impossible to get his Ferrari close enough to Verstappen to try to pass and ended the day frustrated and feeling a win had slipped through his fingers as a consequence of Leclerc's aggression on the first lap. That was a secondary story on the day Antonelli made history, smashing Sebastian Vettel's previous record for being the youngest champion by three years and 67 days. Antonelli also becomes the first Italian to win the F1 title since Alberto Ascari in 1953. Antonelli had tears mixed with laughter over the radio on the slowing down lap as he proved initially incapable of talking when his team told him he was world champion. After he half-composed himself, he said: "Thank you so much. We did it. We did it." The key stories of the race were: Antonelli delivering the title with several races to go in a season he has taken by storm Tension at Ferrari after Leclerc's successful attempts to grab the lead on the first lap led to controversy and unhappiness at the team Verstappen benefiting from the internal battle to take his third win in four races. item.description: Kimi Antonelli has made history by becoming the youngest title winner in the 77th year of the Formula 1 World Championship. The Italian, at 20 years and 68 days, has beaten the record of Sebastian Vettel, who was 23 years and 133 days old when he won the first of his four drivers' championships in 2010. Antonelli, who was still a teenager until 25 August, has secured the title in his second season in the sport. We take a look at F1's other young champions and how Antonelli's achievement compares with theirs. Kimi Antonelli Kimi Antonelli is the youngest F1 world champion and has won nine grands prix since his debut in 2025 [Getty Images] First championship: 2026 Age: 20 years and 68 days Stage of his F1 career when title was won: Second full season F1 debut: 2025 Australian Grand Prix (aged 18) Antonelli has already broken a number of records on the way to becoming F1's youngest champion. In his second season, he became the youngest driver to achieve a pole position in China and the youngest to lead the championship at the next race in Japan. In Monaco, he became the youngest driver to complete a 'grand slam' of pole position, fastest lap, leading every lap and winning the race. All this after a rookie season in 2025 in which there were occasional highs but plenty of errors, and his final total of 150 points was less than half of the 319 accumulated by Mercedes team-mate George Russell. Sebastian Vettel Sebastian Vettel's four drivers' championships were won between 2010-13 [Getty Images] First championship: 2010 Age: 23 years and 133 days Stage of his F1 career when title was won: Third full season F1 debut: 2007 US Grand Prix (aged 19) Vettel was one of four drivers who could win the title going into the season-ending 2010 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix. He was far from the best placed, though, trailing Ferrari's Fernando Alonso by 15 points before the race and his Red Bull team-mate Mark Webber by seven. The German did what he had to do by winning the grand prix and Alonso could only finish seventh, having become stuck behind the Renault of Vitaly Petrov. With Webber in eighth, Vettel won the championship by four points from Alonso. It was yet another F1 record for Vettel. He had become the youngest F1 points scorer on his debut for BMW Sauber in Indianapolis in 2007, before becoming the then youngest pole sitter and race winner at the 2008 Italian Grand Prix for Toro Rosso. item.title: Syracuse football: Orange open as slim underdogs to Clemson
item.description: SYRACUSE, NY - OCTOBER 31: Syracuse Orange Tight End Noah Meyers (81) reacts to scoring the winning touchdown during the second half of the College Football game between the SMU Mustangs and the Syracuse Orange on October 31, 2026, at the JMA Wireless Dome in Syracuse, NY. (Photo by Gregory Fisher/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Syracuse Orange have suddenly improved in their opening odds after a two-game winning streak. Syracuse hosts the Clemson Tigers in the JMA Wireless Dome this Saturday. The Orange only opened as +3.5 point underdogs according to FanDuel’s opening odds . The odds have since decreased as the Orange are only +1.5 point underdogs as of Sunday evening. The Orange are coming off a dramatic win over SMU at home this past Saturday. The Mustangs, then ranked No. 19 at the time, came back from down 10 points at half time to take their first lead of the game with nine minutes left in the game. The Orange kicked a field goal then marched 68 yards down the field on 11 plays in 3:19 to retake the lead with 17 seconds left. The Noah Meyers touchdown was just enough for the Orange to hold on for the upset victory. Steve Angeli threw for 200 yards and the game-winning touchdown on 21-24 passing with no interceptions. He also added a 26-yard rushing touchdown. The Orange defense just barely survived, despite SMU quarterback Kevin Jennings throwing for 352 yards and two touchdowns. The victory gives Syracuse two ACC wins on the season. The Orange had lost its previous 11 ACC games prior to last week. The win also moves Syracuse to a 4-4 record, needing just two wins for bowl eligibility. Clemson got back into the win column with a victory at Florida State. The Tigers scored over 30 points for the first time in ACC play this season as Clemson took down the Seminoles 36-24. The game would be the last that Mike Norvell coached as the leader of Florida State, as he was fired on Sunday afternoon. The Tigers enter the JMA Wireless Dome at 5-3 on the season. Clemson lost at LSU to open the year and also got blown out by Miami. The Tigers also lost to James Franklin’s Virginia Tech team in Death Valley. Syracuse won for the third time in history against Clemson last season. Angeli threw for 245 yards and two touchdowns in the game before tearing his Achilles. Justus Ross-Simmons had two touchdown catches and Johntay Cook had 113 receiving yards as the Orange won 34-21 over the Tigers in Death Valley. Kickoff for Saturday’s marquee matchup is set for 12:00 pm ET. The game will air on ESPN2.

item.title: Lando Norris and Lewis Hamilton lead tributes to talented title winner
item.description: Italian Formula One driver Kimi Antonelli of team Mercedes arrives ahead of the Mexican Formula One Grand Prix at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez. (is associated with: «Lando Norris and Lewis Hamilton lead tributes to talented title winner») Bradley Collyer/PA Wire/dpa Lando Norris hailed the “insane job” Kimi Antonelli has done as the 20-year-old Italian takes over from the British driver as Formula One world champion. Antonelli secured his place in history as F1’s youngest ever champion by finishing third in Mexico City on Sunday. He has blown his competition out of the water, to seal the title with four scheduled rounds still remaining. Norris, who had to come through a final-race battle to clinch his maiden championship in Abu Dhabi last season, believes Antonelli deserves more accolades for his title-winning display. “He’s done an insane job. I feel like people are not giving him enough credit for what he has achieved this year,” Norris said. “He has beaten his team-mate [George Russell] who has been in the sport for four or five times longer than him. Who is also very good and took the battle to Lewis [Hamilton, at Mercedes]. “I think people say ‘he has not had much competition’. That’s because he has slapped his competition! “He’s made it look too easy, like an easy year. If you can make anything look easy nowadays you’ve done an unbelievable job.” Antonelli, then 18, was chosen to replace seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton at Mercedes having joined the team as a 12-year-old. Hamilton, who watched the Italian rise through the ranks, is proud of what Antonelli has achieved. “I think for me, to see a youngster such as Kimi come through from being the little kid standing in the back of the garage, to replacing me at a team that I’ve loved and worked for many, many years and then this year where he’s just been faultless throughout, I think it’s really, really great to see,” Hamilton said. “Records are there to be broken, you know. item.title: Vettel sends emotional message to new youngest F1 champion Antonelli
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Former German race car driver Sebastian Vettel reacts prior to driving Michael Schumacher's 2002 championship winning car ahead of the Italian Grand Prix at the Autodromo Nazionale Monza in Italy. (is associated with: «Vettel sends emotional message to new youngest F1 champion Antonelli») Bradley Collyer/PA Wire/dpa Four-time Formula One world champion Sebastian Vettel sent an emotional message to Kimi Antonelli after the Italian became the sports' youngest-ever champion at 20 years old on Sunday. The German, now retired, was the previous youngest F1 champion. He won his first title at 23 years, 134 days in 2010 with Red Bull. "Kimi, congratulations. World champion. Only very few of us manage to achieve that. And nobody has done it as young as you," Vettel said in a video message published by F1 on X. "You're curious, you listen, you learn fast. You're fearless. Your driving has been very clean and controlled, yet on the limit when it needed to be. You understood that you can only control what you can control," the German added. Vettel said that, when he won his first title, "it all seemed to happen the moment I crossed the finish line." He was overwhelmed and felt like it was impossible to reflect on what he had just done. "I didn't sleep properly for days. So be prepared," Vettel warned. "But I remember the feeling once it sank in. Holding the world championship trophy in my hands and reading all the other champions' names. I felt proud and satisfied." "I realized the best part wasn't crossing the line that decided the title. It was all the races that led to it. It is never the one race that matters. It is all the races we do. Every race shapes us." In the end, Vettel also offered a piece of advice to Antonelli: "Great achievements might change the way people look at you, but you don't have to change the way you look at people. Now go on and enjoy it."

item.title: Jayson Tatum, Paul George lead Boston Celtics to 108-97 win over undermanned Orlando Magic
item.description: The Boston Celtics have historically struggled at the Kia Center, the home of the Orlando Magic . And when it looked like those troubles might continue on Sunday afternoon, the C's came alive down the stretch to secure a 108-97 win on the road. Celtics star Jayson Tatum led the way for Boston once again, notching 32 points (on a game-high 17 attempts from the charity stripe), 7 assists, and 4 rebounds in 34 minutes. He hit multiple big shots for the Green Team in the fourth quarter and assisted on a 3-pointer from Celtics wing Paul George that made it a 106-95 contest with just 1:32 remaining. George finished with 17 points, 8 assists, 6 rebounds, 2 steals, and 2 blocks in the Celtics' first road win of the season. Off the bench, Boston got key contributions from center Luka Garza and wing Baylor Scheierman, who each set season-highs for scoring with 12 points and 10 points, respectively. As for the Magic, guard Anthony Black recorded 23 points and 8 rebounds, helping make up for the absence of guard Jalen Suggs who's out with a bone bruise. Magic forward Tristan da Silva also scored 23 points, using his 5 triples to keep Orlando in the game. Despite his hot shooting, the Magic couldn't overcome losing the turnover battle (18-13) and letting up 21 points off of those mistakes. After defeating the now 2-4 Magic, the Celtics have won five games in a row, tying their longest winning streak from last season. The 5-1 C's will aim to keep that momentum going on Monday night when they travel to Texas to face the 6-1 Houston Rockets . item.description: 🎥 Grêmio take healthy lead in bid for Copa do Brasil final Playing in front of 50,928 fans at a rocking Arena, Grêmio took a strong step toward reaching their tenth Copa do Brasil final. Thanks to goals from Carlos Vinícius and Noriega (and a superb performance from Weverton), the Tricolor beat Atlético Mineiro 2–0 on Sunday (1). It was the first leg of the competition's semi-final. Highlights coming soon. Weverton steals the show in the first half Cuello had a great chance to put Atlético ahead. But he could not beat the Grêmio goalkeeper. Weverton would make another decisive contribution moments later. His goal kick turned into an assist for Carlos Vinícius, who capitalised on a mistake by Lyanco to score (11'). The man behind the assist got plenty of love in the celebrations. Atlético went into the break having dominated possession (over 70%). But Grêmio held firm. With no other option, Barba Domínguez made Galo increasingly attack-minded. Even youngster Cauã Soares, an out-and-out centre-forward, was brought on. Atlético piled on the pressure. And their big chance came in the 94th minute, when Vitor Hugo rattled the crossbar. Gustavo Martins left the Tricolor down to ten men shortly afterwards. item.title: Tributes to 'inspirational' Olympian Ciara Mageean after death at 34
item.description: A statement posted on Mageean's social media on Sunday said she died surrounded by her loved ones [Getty Images] Tributes have been paid to former European champion and two-time Olympic runner Ciara Mageean, who has died at the age of 34. Mageean, from Portaferry in County Down, was diagnosed with stage four bowel cancer in May 2025. She died on Sunday morning, surrounded by her loved ones, a statement posted on her social media accounts said. "A beloved daughter, sister, wife, friend and inspiration to so many, she will be deeply missed," it said. The athlete represented Ireland at the 2016 and 2020 Olympics and won gold in the 1500m at the European Athletics Championships in Rome in 2024. She also represented Northern Ireland at the Commonwealth Games, winning silver in Birmingham in 2022. 'One of our own' Olympic legend Lady Mary Peters said Mageean was a "wonderful lady" who was "gracious, beautiful, talented and inspirational to the next generation". "We knew she was very ill and we knew that it was inevitable but we didn't expect it so soon," said the 1972 Olympic pentathlon gold medallist. Lady Mary's charity the Mary Peters Trust, which supports Northern Ireland athletes, had helped Mageean in her athletics career. "My charity supported her for as long as we could because she was so talented and we recognised that in her," said Lady Mary. She said that Mageean had continued to inspire young athletes even while undergoing treatment for cancer and would be "sorely missed in the world of sport". Mageean won a gold medal at the 2024 European Championships in Rome [EPA] Sean Young, the secretary of Portaferry Gaelic Athletic Club, where Mageean played camogie in her younger years, said its members were in "disbelief and shock" at her death. item.description: Formula One F1 - United States Grand Prix - Circuit of the Americas, Austin, Texas, U.S. - October 25, 2026 Mercedes' Andrea Kimi Antonelli celebrates on the podium after winning the United States Grand Prix IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters/Michael Johnson Formula 1 has a new world champion, and the sport just witnessed history. Kimi Antonelli has officially been crowned the 2026 Formula 1 World Champion , becoming the youngest driver ever to win the championship after finishing third at the Mexican Grand Prix. At just 20 years old, the Mercedes superstar has accomplished something that seemed almost impossible when he first arrived in Formula 1. Antonelli entered the weekend knowing he was on the verge of securing the title. With a massive points advantage over his closest challengers, George Russell and Lewis Hamilton, he only needed a ninth-place finish to guarantee the championship regardless of what his rivals accomplished. And he delivered. Starting fourth, Antonelli kept his composure through a chaotic race that featured a red flag following Valtteri Bottas’ heavy crash and a late safety car. He eventually crossed the line in third place, officially sealing his first career world championship. Max Verstappen took the race victory, with Hamilton finishing second, but the biggest celebration belonged to Antonelli and Mercedes. The achievement is even more impressive when looking at the history he just made. Antonelli has broken Sebastian Vettel’s record as the youngest Formula 1 world champion, taking the crown at just 20 years and 68 days old. He also becomes Italy’s first F1 world champion since Alberto Ascari in 1953. This championship is the result of an incredible second season for the young Italian. After facing plenty of pressure and questions during his rookie campaign, Antonelli has responded with a season that has established him as one of the biggest stars in motorsport. He entered the Mexican Grand Prix with nine victories already under his belt, and now he can add the biggest achievement in racing to his résumé. Mercedes also returns to the top of the Drivers’ Championship for the first time since Lewis Hamilton won the title in 2020. The future of Formula 1 suddenly looks very different. Antonelli has arrived, and he has already taken the biggest prize the sport has to offer. At just 20 years old, Kimi Antonelli is a Formula 1 world champion. And if this season is any indication, this could be the beginning of something special.

item.title: 'We've got big problems' - Hamilton says Ferrari need 'serious talks'
item.description: Lewis Hamilton had to settle for third after securing his first pole position with Ferrari in Mexico [Getty Images] Lewis Hamilton says Ferrari "have to have some serious talks behind closed doors" after fighting between their two drivers cost them victory in the Mexico City Grand Prix. Leclerc cut a chicane on the first lap to take the lead from Hamilton, who then lost second place to Max Verstappen as a consequence of his team-mate's attack. Verstappen went on to win the race with Hamilton second as Kimi Antonelli finished third to become the youngest world champion in Formula 1 history. "Ultimately, that lost us the win today," said Hamilton. "We have to have some serious talks behind closed doors." During a red-flag period in the race caused by a crash for Valtteri Bottas' Cadillac, Hamilton had said over team radio: "We've got big problems. Big, big problems." When informed Hamilton was unhappy, Leclerc said: "I will speak with Lewis. We both didn't make the corner. I don't know if Lewis' point was for me to get P3 but having the Red Bull second I felt it was worth it to keep the position and see what happened. That's what I did. "I could be also unhappy with how much he pushed me off track out of Turn One, but it is racing. When you are fighting for a win it is the way it should be." Hamilton's point is that if the Ferraris had worked together on the first lap, they would have been running one-two and could have controlled the race from there and likely finished in those positions. The incident was the latest and arguably most serious of a series of tensions between Hamilton and Leclerc this season. It follows Leclerc pushing Hamilton off track at the first corner of the Italian Grand Prix. The race before that, Leclerc ignored a team order to let Hamilton by when they were on different strategies. In Singapore last month, there was another incident when Hamilton felt he should have been let by when they were on different tyres, but Ferrari refused to make the call. Verstappen, who capitalised on this latest battle in Mexico, said: "Ferrari were really fast, I do think they made it a little bit difficult for themselves fighting each other and that's why I was able to capitalise on that. I mean, I take it, right? More to follow. item.description: Man United set for crunch talks with Lisandro Martinez to decide his fate after Chelsea horror show Despite dominating Chelsea in the first half, Manchester United returned home empty-handed from Stamford Bridge on Saturday. It was his defensive error that allowed Morgan Rogers to open the scoring for the hosts, while he earned a red card and gave away a penalty to seal the deal. The Argentine has been angling for a move away for some time now, and coupled with his incendiary comments aimed at the sporting director and his recent displays, it makes sense for INEOS to cut him loose. Barcelona , Atletico Madrid and three Serie A teams are chasing the World Cup winner ‘s signature, with his current deal up next summer. But the 20-time English league champions do hold the option of triggering a one-year extension so as to not allow the centre-back’s value to drop. What step United’s co-owners will eventually take will be decided later this month, with Fabrizio Romano revealing that a meeting between Lisandro Martinez and INEOS is expected in November. “It’s not an easy moment for Lisandro Martínez in general. His contract is up in June 2027, so at the end of this season, Manchester United have a club option to extend it until 2028. INEOS could grant him his wish “The information I’m getting is that, this month, over the next few days and weeks, there will be direct contacts between Lisandro Martínez’s camp and Manchester United to assess the situation and consider all the possibilities: exercising the option, not exercising it, leaving the club or staying. “There will be discussions on several points, including his attitude, performances, future and contract situation. So, talks are expected to take place regarding Lisandro Martínez’s future.” It is not a straightforward call given the dearth of quality at the back. Matthijs de Ligt has only just returned from long-term injury and he needs more time. Both Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven have been utilised out wide more than at the heart of the defence. Losing Lisandro Martinez would mean a lot of extra pressure on Harry Maguire. item.title: Should NASCAR Step In After Carson Hocevar’s Controversial Brake Checks End Austin Cindric’s Day at Martinsville?
item.description: Nov 1, 2026; Martinsville, Virginia, USA; Spire Motorsports driver Carson Hocevar (77) signs autographs before the NASCAR Cup Series Xfinity 500 at Martinsville Speedway. Mandatory Credit: Greg Atkins-Imagn Images ASCAR has a serious decision to make after Sunday’s race at Martinsville Speedway, and Carson Hocevar could find himself facing consequences. The Spire Motorsports driver became the center of controversy during the Xfinity 500 after appearing to brake-check Austin Cindric multiple times, ultimately causing significant damage to the No. 2 Ford and ending Cindric’s race early. And Cindric wasn’t happy about it. The incident unfolded during Stage 2 after Hocevar spun on his own and reported over the radio that his car was undriveable. On the following restart, Hocevar appeared to slow abruptly in front of Cindric on the frontstretch, then did it again exiting Turn 2. A third brake check proved to be too much for Cindric, who made contact with the back of Hocevar’s Chevrolet. The damage was severe enough that the No. 2 team had to remove the hood while attempting repairs before eventually taking the car to the garage. Cindric made his frustration clear over the team radio. “NASCAR, what are we doing? Like, we’re just weaponizing cars here. I stack on entry with the guy and he has a mental breakdown.” And he wasn’t the only one questioning Hocevar’s actions. Other teams also expressed frustration over the radio, with Christopher Bell’s crew chief Adam Stevens and Austin Dillon both questioning whether Hocevar’s earlier spin was intentional. This situation raises an even bigger question about NASCAR’s responsibility to police aggressive driving. Hocevar has developed a reputation for being one of the most aggressive drivers in the Cup Series. He has been involved in several controversial incidents over the past few seasons, including confrontations with Ryan Blaney and Austin Cindric. NASCAR has previously handed Hocevar penalties for on-track incidents, including a $50,000 fine and a 25-point deduction in 2024 after an incident with Harrison Burton. But should repeated brake checks that put another driver’s equipment and safety at risk result in a more serious punishment? There is a difference between hard racing and deliberately slowing down in front of another competitor. Drivers are expected to race aggressively, but using a race car to retaliate can create dangerous situations for everyone involved. The timing makes this even more interesting. Martinsville was the final race before the championship finale at Homestead, and Cindric was left with a damaged car and a disappointing result. NASCAR now has an opportunity to review the footage and decide whether further action is necessary.
